stimulus.text:
The Selective Service Act, approved May 18, 1917, Section 5 (verbatim excerpts):

"That all male persons between the ages of twenty-one and thirty, both inclusive, shall be subject to registration in accordance with regulations to be prescribed by the President . . . it shall be the duty of all persons of the designated ages . . . to present themselves for and submit to registration under the provisions of this Act; and any person who shall wilfully fail or refuse to present himself for registration or to submit thereto as herein provided, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor . . ."
stimulus.source_note: Verbatim excerpts from the Selective Service Act, May 18, 1917, Section 5 (public domain).

rationales.A: The law orders men to register and punishes refusal. That is not asking for volunteers only.
rationales.B: The law registers men inside the United States. It says nothing about hiring foreign soldiers.
rationales.C: Every man aged 21 to 30 had to register, and refusal was a crime. That is a national draft, run by the government.
rationales.D: The law registers men aged 21 to 30, not veterans of an earlier war.
rationales.general:
1. Read what the law orders. All men aged 21 to 30 must register.
2. Read the penalty. Refusal is a misdemeanor, so registration is not a choice.
3. Note the ages. The law names men from 21 to 30, the ages the government wanted for its new army.
4. Name the system. A required national list of men is a draft.
Remember: when a law orders an action and punishes refusal, the action is required, not voluntary.
